key_insight: Adaptive, relevance-aware context management—keeping different parts of an agent's trajectory at different levels of detail—lets long-horizon search agents scale without accumulating prohibitive cost or error-prone clutter.
problem_solved: Prevents unbounded growth of intermediate context in long-horizon search agents, which otherwise increases runtime cost, latency, and the probability of reasoning errors.
method: Context-ReAct: orchestrates an elastic context store that maintains trajectory elements at multiple resolutions (full, summarized, archived) based on current task relevance.
Relevance-scoring + adaptive compression: continuously score past observations/actions and compress or demote low-relevance items while preserving reconstructability for on-demand retrieval.
On-demand reconstruction & selective retrieval: retrieve or expand stored summaries when relevance changes so the agent keeps only the needed detail in working memory.
impact: Reduces compute and memory overhead for long-running agents and lowers error rates caused by noisy or irrelevant context, making large-scale, long-horizon search systems more efficient and reliable.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: agent loop showing actions → context bank with tiers (full detail, summarized, archived) → retrieval/backfill to the agent.
Before/After chart: context size and token cost over time for naive accumulation vs. elastic orchestration.
Timeline visualization: agent trajectory with variable-resolution blocks (thick = full detail, thin = summary) illustrating selective retention.
Tradeoff icon/plot: relevance threshold vs. cost vs. accuracy to show tuning of compression/retrieval policies.
paper_title: LongSeeker: Elastic Context Orchestration for Long-Horizon Search Agents
paper_authors: Yijun Lu, Rui Ye, Yuwen Du, Jiajun Wang, Songhua Liu
